title: Do Women Need to Stop Eating Rice to Lose Weight?
intro: No need. You can lose weight while still eating rice, as long as your portion and the dishes you pair it with are right.

sections.p: You lose weight when the calories you take in are slightly less than what your body uses. Rice is just one source of calories. Usually what makes calories shoot up is extra rice, lots of gravy, fried food and sweet drinks.
One cup of white rice is about 200 calories (estimate). For many women who want to lose weight, half to one cup per meal is enough. An easy way: take a portion of rice the size of your fist.

sections.h: Arrange your plate at the nasi campur shop
sections.p: Imagine your plate divided into sections. A quarter for rice, a quarter for protein like chicken, fish, egg or tofu. The other half for vegetables. Ask for less gravy or have it on the side.

sections.h: What about nasi lemak and nasi goreng?
sections.p: Nasi lemak, nasi goreng and biryani are higher in calories because of the santan or oil. You can still eat them. What matters is how often and how much, for example 1-2 times a week with a protein dish and vegetables.

action: This week, try taking a fist-sized portion of rice every time you eat.
When you buy nasi campur, make sure you have one protein and two types of vegetables.
Ask for less gravy or 'kuah asing' (gravy on the side) at the shop.
Swap one sweet drink a day for plain water or teh O kosong.
myth: Many people believe eating rice at night turns straight into fat. In reality, your total calories for the whole day matter more than what time you eat rice.

faq.q: Is brown rice better for weight loss?
faq.a: Brown rice has about the same calories as white rice. Its advantage is more fibre, so it may keep you full longer. Choose the one you like and can keep eating.

faq.q: Can I eat rice at night?
faq.a: Yes. If you have a late dinner because of traffic, take a smaller portion and add more vegetables and protein.

faq.q: I have PCOS or high blood sugar. Do I need to cut down on rice?
faq.a: Everyone's needs are different. Please check with your doctor or dietitian about the right amount of carbohydrates for your condition.
